bio: Dual-degree student in Digital Engineering & Management at UTC and EDHEC Business School, majoring in Data & Finance. After six months as a CRM Data Analyst at Nespresso, I want to deepen my data science and modelling skills in an MSc in Data Science & Business Analytics starting in 2027.

about: My background brings together three complementary dimensions: a dual engineering (UTC) and management (EDHEC) education, an international outlook built between France, Germany and China, and a quantitative foundation in econometrics, machine learning and finance. I have applied these methods to concrete projects, from the predictability of Brent oil returns to predicting bank customers' behaviour, credit scoring and a geospatial analysis of Shanghai real estate. In industry, as a CRM Data Analyst at Nespresso, I built KPIs and dashboards and turned analyses into recommendations. An MSc in Data Science & Business Analytics is the natural next step for me to deepen my modelling and machine learning skills in support of business and financial decisions.

projects.title: Can Brent oil be predicted day to day?
projects.subtitle: Econometrics — Brent oil returns
projects.description: Does yesterday's return help explain today's, and does that relationship change in the tails of the distribution?
projects.method: Daily Brent log-returns from 1987 to 2020, simple and multiple OLS on past returns, joint F-test, heteroskedasticity diagnostics and quantile regressions (τ from 0.1 to 0.9) in R.
projects.results: Mean predictability is close to zero: yesterday's return barely explains today's. The dynamics run mostly through volatility, which points towards GARCH models.
projects.photo_alt: Daily Brent price in US dollars per barrel, 1987 to 2020

projects.title: Designing a database from scratch
projects.subtitle: Community Management System — PostgreSQL & Python
projects.description: A platform connecting people and communities: memberships, messaging, skills, shared services and exclusion votes.
projects.method: From conceptual model to logical schema: 12 PostgreSQL tables, Entity → Individual / Community inheritance, integrity enforced through keys, UNIQUE and CHECK constraints. Business views, a recursive query that rebuilds message threads, GPS distance between members and safe transactions.
projects.results: A consistent, working database driven by two Python interfaces (admin and user, psycopg2 and Tkinter) and populated by a test-data generator.

projects.title: Predicting and segmenting a bank's customers
projects.subtitle: Data Mining & Machine Learning — Bank Marketing
projects.description: Out of 40,000+ customers, identify those who will subscribe to a term deposit, despite highly imbalanced classes.
projects.method: Exploratory analysis (only 11% of customers subscribe), scikit-learn pipeline with scaling and one-hot encoding, logistic regression evaluated with 5-fold stratified cross-validation, then K-Means segmentation (elbow method, k = 3).
projects.results: ROC AUC of 0.94 and 71% precision on subscribers. Segmentation reveals a group of customers already contacted in previous campaigns with a 63% subscription rate, versus 5% for the largest segment: the bank should prioritise these follow-ups.

projects.title: Predicting a customer's credit score
projects.subtitle: Machine learning — credit scoring
projects.description: Using 100,000 financial and personal records, classify each customer's credit score as Good, Standard or Poor, a core risk-assessment task in banking.
projects.method: Cleaning noisy data (stray characters, inconsistent values, credit history converted to months), exploratory analysis by class, one-hot encoding, imputation and scaling, then a multinomial logistic regression evaluated with log-loss and F1-score.
projects.results: 73% correct predictions across three classes (macro F1 of 0.71, log-loss of 0.715). Outstanding debt and payment delays are the most influential variables.

projects.title: Does the subway push up property prices in Shanghai?
projects.subtitle: Geospatial analysis and regression — real estate
projects.description: Matching 450,000 property listings with subway entrances to measure how proximity to a station affects the price per square metre.
projects.method: Cleaning and geographic filtering of the listings (Anjuke, 2017), extraction of subway entrances from a points-of-interest database (Gaode), vectorised distance to the nearest entrance with GeoPandas and Shapely, then an OLS regression of price per m² on distance with residual analysis.
projects.results: A negative, highly significant effect: about −2 ¥/m² per metre away from the subway, or −2,000 ¥/m² per kilometre. Distance alone explains only 17.5% of the variance, and residuals show strong spatial autocorrelation, pointing to next steps (distance to the centre, district effects).
